module_title: Introduction to the Planning Commission and NDC
introduction: After independence, India needed a central direction to utilize its limited resources effectively. Inspired by the Soviet Union (USSR), the government established the Planning Commission. At this level, we will understand its basic structure and status.

core_concepts.title: Establishment of the Planning Commission
core_concepts.description: The Planning Commission was set up on 'March 15, 1950', via an Executive Resolution of the Union Cabinet. Its formation was heavily based on the recommendations of the 'K.C. Neogy Committee' (1946).

core_concepts.title: Constitutional Status
core_concepts.description: This is the most critical exam point: The Planning Commission was neither a 'Constitutional Body' (no mention in the Constitution) nor a 'Statutory Body' (not created by an Act of Parliament). It was purely an extra-constitutional, advisory body.

core_concepts.title: Structure
core_concepts.description: The Prime Minister of India served as the 'Ex-officio Chairman' of the Planning Commission. The 'First Chairman' was Jawaharlal Nehru, and the 'First Deputy Chairman' was Gulzarilal Nanda. The last Deputy Chairman was Montek Singh Ahluwalia.

core_concepts.title: National Development Council (NDC)
core_concepts.description: The Planning Commission only drafted the plans; it could not enforce them. The NDC was established on 'August 6, 1952', to give the final approval to the Five-Year Plans. It included the Chief Ministers of all states to ensure states' participation. The PM was also the Chairman of the NDC.

important_entities.name: NDC - The 'Super Cabinet'
important_entities.significance: Eminent economist K. Santhanam famously referred to the NDC as the 'Super Cabinet' because no Five-Year Plan could be implemented until the NDC gave its final nod.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Question: 'Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body? A) Election Commission B) Finance Commission C) UPSC D) Planning Commission.' The answer is always 'Planning Commission' (or NITI Aayog), as it has no constitutional article assigned to it.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The Planning Commission was created first (1950) to draft the plans. The NDC was created later (1952) to pass and approve those plans.

exam_strategy_tips: The exact date of the Planning Commission's establishment, '15 March 1950', is repeatedly asked as a direct trivia question in SSC, Railways, and State PCS exams.
